name: detect-speech-segments
summary: Score one 32ms window of 16kHz mono audio for human-speech risk using a real Silero VAD model forward pass.
description: A single-chunk speech-risk scorer: given exactly 512 samples (32ms) of 16kHz mono PCM plus the model's own carried streaming state (a 64-sample audio context and an LSTM (h,c) pair, all optional -- default to a cold start), runs one real Silero VAD (snakers4/silero-vad, MIT) forward pass -- reflect-pad, an STFT-as-Conv1d front end, a 4-layer Conv1d+ReLU encoder, one LSTMCell step, a final Conv1d, and a sigmoid -- and returns a speech probability plus the updated context/state to carry into the next chunk. It does not chunk a whole recording, apply a decision threshold, merge adjacent windows into segments, or decide anything about export/sharing -- that is a caller-owned policy over a stream of these scores (mirrors how classifier.release-gate-evaluate and classification.outcome-resolve keep policy separate from scoring). It does not resample audio, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow. On malformed input it fails closed: status is invalid_input and speech_probability is 1.0 (maximum caution), never a false all-clear.

use_cases.scenario: As an audio operator, I want a quiet or silent window scored with low speech probability, so that a caller's downstream policy can let genuinely quiet audio through.

As an audio operator, I want the model's own streaming context and LSTM state threaded from one window's output into the next window's input, so that scoring a real recording chunk by chunk matches scoring it in one pass.
As an audio operator, I want a window of the wrong length rejected with maximum-caution output rather than silently scored, so that a malformed chunk can never look like verified-safe audio.
As an audio operator, I want a malformed carried-context array rejected even when the new samples are valid, so that a corrupted streaming state can never silently reset to a false all-clear.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies exactly 512 samples of 16kHz mono PCM; context/state_h/state_c are optional and default to a cold start (all zeros) when absent.

postconditions.description: Any malformed samples/context/state_h/state_c yields status=invalid_input and speech_probability=1.0 (never a false all-clear).

Identical (samples, context, state_h, state_c) always yields identical output within one WASM instantiation. Cross-instantiation / cross-host-architecture byte-identity is NOT proven -- see risk.determinism_class.

side_effects.description: Produces a probability and updated streaming state in memory; does not log, persist, or transmit audio.

provenance.author: enricopiovesan
provenance.spec_ref: registry#460, follow-up to #455 (second spec 001 FR-017 agent). Motivated by enricopiovesan/Callweave, which fails closed on external review of field recordings pending local speech detection (README.md / DECISION_RECORD.md D-019) and has already vendored this exact model (models/silero-vad/, MIT, SHA256-pinned) but never wired it into its pipeline. Published generically under audio.* rather than callweave.* so any Traverse app can consume it via registry_ref, the same way Callweave already consumes classifier.release-gate-evaluate.

authoring.test_evidence: capability-src/audio-detect-speech-segments: 15 #[test] cases (VAD1 header parse, bad-magic rejection, reflect-pad-right correctness, forward-pass finiteness/range/determinism/differs-by-input, context-carries-last-samples, fail-closed on missing/wrong-length samples and on malformed context even with valid samples, context/state threading across two calls, f32-array round-trip, sigmoid bounds) against a synthetic fixture at the model's real fixed dimensions; cargo llvm-cov functions=100%, lines=98.22%, regions=97.48%. Separately verified end to end against the real published ONNX graph (snakers4/silero-vad src/silero_vad/data/silero_vad_16k_op15.onnx) via onnxruntime: extracted intermediate tensors (magnitude spectrogram, each encoder layer) to pin down the exact reflect-pad-right(64) / real-imaginary channel split before writing any Rust, then ran the actual built --features full-model artifact under wasmtime across a chained 6-chunk sequence with context/state threaded exactly as the model's own upstream OnnxWrapper.__call__ does -- output matched the real ONNX model to 4 decimal places on every chunk (0.0017/0.1648/0.7735/0.7455/0.8590/0.1593, both sides identical). Not quantized: per-tensor int8 on the LSTM gates was tested and measurably breaks output (max|probability diff| ~0.9 vs the real graph over a 20-chunk sequence, because hidden state carries quantization error forward across every subsequent chunk) -- shipped as plain float32 instead (~1.2 MB, small enough that quantizing wasn't needed for size anyway). Cross-arch (x86_64 vs aarch64) byte-identity was NOT verified -- no x86_64 host or emulator was available in the authoring environment -- hence risk.determinism_class: model_derived rather than deterministic (spec 024). License: snakers4/silero-vad is MIT, verified directly against the repository's own LICENSE file.
